approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from score-ranked survivors, using crossover and local mutations to make fresh candidate pools. It rejects duplicate identities and sulfur environments that exceed the maximum present in the original scored parents. A Gaussian process learns from every accepted observation using chiral local-environment counts and count-sensitive Tanimoto similarity. Each batch selects masked maxima of correlated sampled values, combining the learned mean with a shared count-GP residual law; accepted offspring then enter the archive and compete for the next breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace the successful allocator's predictive mean with one frozen synthetic-pretrained TabPFN-3.5 model that sees every count coordinate through its native magnitude, Fourier and empirical-rank encoders. Keep the original correlated GP residual and graph search. Earlier siblings tested a projected older tabular model, a molecular-embedding mean blend, tree functions and altered breeding policies. This fixed revision instead tests native full-coordinate contextual prediction with the wide-table prior, while preserving the Parent environment. It jointly changes the external input/encoder/prior recipe; it does not establish why the older projection recipe failed.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is weak absolute productive exploration despite useful learned direction. Actual Parent summaries and run logs complete all three assigned replicas and all fifteen endpoints, with mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878, all proposal validity 1 and duplicate rejection rate 0. The full Parent stream has 648 strict best-parent wins among 4350 offspring, summed positive margins 17.25153528627184 and summed sequential incumbent gain 5.819415048695712. n-37a4fc183d94 delivered 691 newly supported champions and 1795 accepted descendants but increased local wins to 738 while lowering gain magnitudes and the matched mean by 0.055186727444823. n-04741f9b1832 removed only candidate-dependent GP location: all 435 original mean pools were nonconstant, 3733 strict choices changed, and all fifteen endpoints fell (mean -0.182967629428378). The original mean therefore supplies valuable conditional direction, not a missing-path problem. n-3062f0c87203 exposed a fixed projected TabPFN-v2 recipe but same-label pair ordering was 0.6349149415863906 versus passive GP 0.6893830703012912 and Spearman 0.35278052022601825 versus 0.48433302836152137. Its Anchor comparison remains cross-lock unpaired. n-fe734eb5c1df retains all external work and removes only that active location under its exact lock, gaining 0.05167897370782667 with fourteen endpoint gains and one loss: negative contribution of that fixed old recipe, without projection/prior/preprocessing attribution or independent replication. Separate current-Parent location-only and residual-only count removals n-161b32768a03/n-b77e5493be1e lose 0.08822718632415433/0.03715967951388403, supporting their conditional count consumers. The fully exposed n-61c472c961cc molecular-feature blend also loses ranking and 0.06811086167142866. These observations support a single test of a substantively different native-count predictive-location recipe; none predicts its efficacy as a fact.

finding_summary.headline: Native contextual predictions changed search but weakened ranking, productive gains and final scores
finding_summary.insights: This result rules out absent model exposure, omitted count coordinates, lost accepted-context rows, altered residual draws and construction infeasibility as explanations for this recipe’s failure. Exact-source execution and richer native count input did not make the external predictor a better guide than the original GP on the selected molecular candidates. The extra local wins came against weaker parents, and greater scaffold breadth did not translate into larger useful gains. The chemistry audit helps explain why breadth is an inadequate proxy: some streams enlarged or repeated familiar fragments, while fewer direct N/O–halogen bonds coexisted with more sulfur–nitrogen connections and difficult ring topologies. Those output associations do not identify a chemical cause of the loss. The current exact-lock comparison supports a negative contribution from the whole fixed native-location recipe under this retained search composition; it cannot separate encoding, prior, preprocessing or hybrid-residual effects, diagnose the earlier projected recipe, or establish ranking-mediated causation. The registered complete adverse-result condition is met, so this fixed recipe stops. A checkpoint, width, permutation, precision, target-transform, blend or archive-window sweep is not a justified continuation.
finding_summary.results: The native predictor operated in all 15 sessions, producing 435 nonconstant full-coordinate prediction pools. It changed 2,834 of 4,350 accepted choices; 775 of those changed sources later produced 2,510 accepted descendants. The substitution therefore reached both learning and breeding. On the same actual labels, however, pairwise ordering accuracy fell from the original GP’s 0.698242 to 0.657184, and mean batch Spearman fell from 0.505819 to 0.402270. Both ranking measures were worse in every early/middle/late phase, and no task/seed session improved both. Mean accepted score fell from 0.372050 to 0.323251. There were slightly more parent-beating offspring (654 versus 648), but their summed positive gain fell from 17.251535 to 14.377969 and sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.819415 to 4.683073. More productive alternative cores entered breeding, yet their descendants delivered less gain. The complete matched final-score mean was 0.520697 versus 0.596453, a change of −0.075756 against the required +0.002. Thirteen of fifteen endpoints declined; seed 1’s macro and two individual endpoints improved. Population standard deviation increased from 0.033970 to 0.058846. All runs completed within the issued resources without model warnings or fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output spans recognizable aryl amines, oversized repeated cores, reactive attachments and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-5277bf3b7425 produces aromatic carbonyl compounds, nitrogen-rich fused systems, aryl-linked amines, medium-ring lactams and fluorinated diones. These are not ring-poor fragments: the digest reports molecule-level ring-closure-text incidence 0.9471–1.0 and aromatic-text incidence 0.8943–1.0. Those string incidences are not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. All task digests have zero explicit charge and stereocentre-string incidence; neutral notation does not imply absence of basic centres. The output combines recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments with difficult complete topologies and reactive local bonds, supporting rich ring/aromatic chemistry but questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. The diversity judgment is moderate: different sessions reach distinct families and numerous cores, but leaders within sessions repeatedly decorate related arrangements, and scaffold counts include strained or oversized structures. All 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories were present and read. Each node supplies 900 records per task, including 870 accepted optimizer observations; all 9000 records parse with RDKit 2023.09.6. There are no missing paths, uncovered tasks or absent paired seeds. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile-mismatched seeds. No complete Child session exactly reproduces its paired Parent evaluation/source/SMILES/score/best_so_far sequence. The Parent comparison includes the late seed-0 evaluation-281 breakthrough, rather than truncating that history. Every score quoted below is a supplied accepted-record label. Best examples are taken from the full sessions; digest final examples are last proposals, not endpoint winners. Computed quantities are descriptive readings of those same trajectories: heavy atoms, RDKit ring basis, explicit bond flags, unassigned stereocentre perception and typed/generic Bemis–Murcko cores. Deciles each contain 87 optimizer observations per task pooled across seeds; they describe the observed stream and can be dominated by one seed. Empty cores and repeated observations across sessions are retained. Across 4350 optimizer observations, Child versus Parent has 544 versus 786 with direct N-halogen bonds, 89 versus 217 with O-halogen bonds, 86 versus 93 with S-halogen bonds and 101 versus 127 with O–O single bonds. At the same time, S–N bonds occur in 1050 versus 306 observations and sulfur in 1706 versus 1100. These categories overlap and are structural flags, not a toxicity, instability or synthesis score; conventional sulfonamides and N–O groups are not automatically liabilities. Child has 2464 observations with perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres versus Parent 2455; neither has assigned centres in optimizer output under this audit. Raw core breadth does not establish productive exploration, and fewer reactive-looking bonds do not establish a component benefit. The chemistry associations here do not decide mechanism activation, causal mediation, endpoint success or selection. Full descriptor definitions, per-record provenance and hashes of all trusted source files are in .slots/L01-resume-20261004/r34-slot0-molecular/chemistry_statistics.json and molecule_descriptors.jsonl. The exact immutable request is r0034-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-92e84ddfc41b0bd9.json. Parent chemistry was checked against its published trajectories and indexed policy-node assessment; no confirmation-seed or external target-answer evidence was used.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds: optimizer median 25.5 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, versus Parent 24 and three. Seed 0 ends best with a 25-heavy-atom methoxy/fluoromethyl benzene fused to an unsaturated N–N ring, linked through a ketone/methylene unit to chloropyridine. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom, five-ring indole-derived carboxamide containing an additional fused NH ring and a constrained aryl-linked N–O ring on the amide nitrogen. Seed 2 reaches a more recognizable 26-heavy-atom indole anilide bearing nitrile, methoxy, methylthio and aryl fluorine. The high-score decile has 23–26 heavy atoms and a median of three aromatic rings. Sulfur-containing observations rise from Parent 251 to Child 461, and S–N-containing observations from 28 to 264; those counts do not classify every sulfur environment as problematic. The seed-2 indole amide looks more conventionally approachable than the constrained N–O ring and hydrazine-like alternatives, but no route or stability has been demonstrated.
liabilities: The leading constrained aryl N–O ring and the separate unsaturated N–N-ring family warrant local geometry and stability assessment; an N–O bond alone is not sufficient to call a molecule implausible.

High-label relatives include S–N/extended sulfur attachments, while late molecules include chloromethyl ethers and halomethyl substituents. These are different environments from the more ordinary methylthio group of the seed-2 best.
missing_features: Repeated high-label realizations of the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement with conventional local bonding are limited: the best seed introduces a constrained N–O heterocycle, whereas the ordinary indole amide in another seed remains lower labelled.

There is no demonstrated shortage of aromatic rings, carbonyl groups, amines or sulfur. The observed labels do not identify an exact missing target scaffold or establish that the N–O closure itself is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.4145039882261785, 0.4531634835874829 and 0.4108837967205422; Parent best scores are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. The seed-1 label is associated with compact aromatic/carbonyl organization and ring closure, not simply larger size: an extended indole/anilide/thiourea/pyrazoline assembly at seed 2 evaluation 20 scores 3.315183114286997e-17, while FCl scores 0.0. The seed-2 nitrile/methylthio indole shows that direct heteroatom–halogen bonds are unnecessary for a useful label. Direct N-halogen observations fall from Parent 275 to Child 78, and from 53 to 8 in the respective high-score deciles, without restoring the Parent labels. This is a change in chemical realization, not evidence that removing N-halogen bonds caused the score difference. The seed-2 final proposal scores 0.1819589039685845 and is not its best molecule.

per_task.generated_character: The most conspicuous change is size and repeated ring architecture: optimizer median 50 heavy atoms versus Parent 31, with Child range 9–120 and median five rings. Seed 0 repeatedly joins azaaromatic units, aryl oxygen bridges and carbonyl/ester linkers. Its evaluation-291 best has 108 heavy atoms, 24 perceived rings and 27 rotatable bonds; the ring basis includes eight four-membered rings, so this is a highly elaborate repeated assembly rather than an ordinary compact heterocycle. Seed 1 instead gives a 34-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring azaaryl/imidazole-like system with urea/acyl/formyl connectivity, vinyl substitution, aryl halogens and a terminal C=S group. Seed 2 gives a 47-heavy-atom N–N-linked pair of fused diones with imine-containing side chains and a cyanoacetate ester. These disparate families show that large repeats are one session outcome, not a universal requirement. The Parent best in seed 0 is much smaller, with 30 heavy atoms and five perceived rings; it still contains O–F and halomethyl ether liabilities.
liabilities: The seed-0 best combines very large size and many rotatable bonds with repeated four-membered aryl-oxygen/carbon bridges. That combination raises substantial synthetic and conformational questions; perceived ring closure is not an accessible geometry demonstration.

The smaller seed-1 family carries terminal thiocarbonyl and dense acyl/formyl functionality; seed 2 carries imine-rich substituents and N–N-linked diones. These require environment-specific assessment and cannot be called stable simply because they lack the large repeats.
Direct N-halogen observations increase from Parent 39 to Child 97 even though neither high-score decile contains them; these bonds do not explain the leading score gradient.
missing_features: A compact, independently realized high-label arrangement comparable to the published Parent seed-0 example is absent from these Child trajectories. Merely accumulating azaaromatic rings and carbonyls does not reproduce it.

Chemically credible connectivity with bounded repetition remains unresolved in the leading large family. The scores do not identify an exact missing target feature or establish that any individual ester, imine or oxygen bridge is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A small halophenol at seed 1 evaluation 13 scores 0.5052914719111032; the seed-0 peroxide/azaaryl proposal at evaluation 15 scores 0.5100965759438103. Child best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.6120904387813757, 0.6080498792191682 and 0.5931410227426867. Parent reaches 0.8561477222467935 at seed 0 evaluation 281, then 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496 in the other seeds. Within Child, the high-score decile has median 78 heavy atoms versus 31 in the low-score decile; Parent high-score decile median is only 32. Thus this Child stream rewards certain repeated heterocyclic/carbonyl combinations locally, but the paired evidence does not support a general need for extreme size. Even the much smaller Child seed-1 leader approaches the repeated assembly label. Distinct generic cores among all optimizer observations are Child 361 versus Parent 240, and among high-score deciles 50 versus 9; this is structural breadth, not evidence of useful scaffold delivery or component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: The output is strongly aryl/halogen-rich and contains readily recognizable aliphatic amine regions, but the complete arrangements differ sharply by seed. Optimizer median size is 36 heavy atoms versus Parent 29. The Child seed-1 best has 30 heavy atoms and four rings: a tertiary methylamine connecting a substituted cyclohexadiene/azaaryl region and a chloroaryl methyl sulfoxide. Its azaaryl ring also has a three-membered oxygen bridge across an aromatic bond, a major geometric concern despite an otherwise recognizable amine layout. Seed 2 supplies a comparatively conventional 27-heavy-atom biaryl bearing phenol, methoxy, aryl fluorine, a primary aminomethyl group and a saturated six-membered diaza ring; its shared carbon between nitrogens still gives an aminal environment to assess. Seed 0 remains a 36-heavy-atom highly halogenated ketone/imine/unsaturated eight-membered nitrogen-ring family with an aryl S–N substituent. The high-score decile has median 33 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings; its molecules all satisfy the stated crude aliphatic-amine structural flag, which is not a pKa prediction.
liabilities: The three-membered bridge over an aromatic bond and additional unsaturated small-ring analogues require geometric assessment; ordinary aromatic content does not establish a feasible conformer.
Late accepted examples add peroxide or O-halogen functionality and complex N–O/N–N rings. The comparatively conventional seed-2 best is a counterexample to needing those additions.

Sulfur rises from Parent 254 to Child 650 observations, and S–N bonds from 156 to 455. Much of that population includes sulfonyl chemistry; this is an environment distribution, not evidence that every S–N bond is reactive.
missing_features: The generator already produces basic-amine-like centres; the missing capability is consistent delivery of their favorable aromatic arrangement without the difficult oxygen-bridged small ring or heavily substituted imine/sulfur family.

Defined stereochemical forms are absent: 863 of 870 Child optimizer observations and all 87 in the high-score decile have perceived unassigned centres. The seed-2 best has two; the sulfoxide-bearing seed-1 best has one. Score effects of resolving them were not tested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small N-sulfonyl cyclic ketone at seed 0 evaluation 20 scores 0.00021169315013374197 and the seed-2 dichloroanisole scores 0.0022311965578061463. Child best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.5058320932595909, 0.9845950718171165 and 0.972113099664767, versus Parent 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. The observed gradient is consistent with suitable amine presentation alongside aromatic regions rather than halogen mass, sulfur or nitrogen count alone. The much lower seed-0 family already contains nitrogen and aromatic rings, so merely adding these groups is not an established solution. The seed-2 best has no sulfur, direct N/O-halogen bond or small unsaturated ring, demonstrating a high-label alternative to the seed-1 oxygen-bridged azaarene. Child has 148 observations with a three-membered ring containing two aromatic atoms versus none in Parent; 44 of the Child high-score decile carry that topology. The labels therefore do not exclude this liability. No affinity, protonation, safety, stereoselectivity or synthetic-accessibility conclusion follows from these accepted labels.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl and ether frameworks become densely connected medium-ring systems. Optimizer median is 33 heavy atoms and five rings versus Parent 31 and four. Seed 0 best has 38 heavy atoms and two nine-membered rings, with aryl ether/N-methylamine connectivity and an unsaturated link to an N–O/carbonyl-containing ring. Seed 1 best has 35 heavy atoms and a ring basis containing four-, seven- and eleven-membered closures alongside its aromatic rings; N–N/N–O connections and multiple carbonyl groups add further local complexity. Seed 2 best has 33 heavy atoms and five rings: a fused aryl/azaaryl/ether system attached to an N-methyl lactam, with alkyl and ethoxy substituents. Its largest perceived rings are seven and eight members. These are elaborate, potentially stereogenic frameworks, with no route or conformational evidence. Raw typed/generic core counts are Child 510/310 versus Parent 585/392; numerous identities do not remove the recurring connected-ring character.
liabilities: Medium and larger rings are not intrinsically implausible, but these multiply connected, partly unsaturated N–N/N–O frameworks require explicit geometry and route assessment.

Late proposals include a three-membered cyclic ester and related small cyclic carbonyl appendages. The label tolerance of these structures is separate from whether they are viable medicinal compounds.
missing_features: Simpler chemically credible versions of the favorable aromatic/carbonyl relationship are not consistently recovered at the leading labels; replacing functional organization with additional closures is not shown to help.

Stereochemical and conformational specification of the connected-ring leaders is missing: all 87 high-score-decile observations have perceived unassigned centres, compared with 57 in the Parent high-score decile.
There is no shortage of aromatic rings, carbonyl groups or heteroatoms. The molecules do not support prescribing a particular target scaffold from this trajectory alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The smaller fluoroacetanilide and carboxyacetyl anilide score 0.07615914142616902 and 0.07504633196017493. Child best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.22469491511391348, 0.20763082877093567 and 0.22748035481763473; Parent scores are 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. The observed gradient favors complete aromatic/heteroatom/carbonyl arrangements over small isolated amides, but the high-score decile median grows from Parent 30 to Child 36 heavy atoms without a consistent label advantage across seeds. The seed-2 late analogue bearing a tiny cyclic ester at evaluation 295 still scores 0.21915824179890764, below its 0.22748035481763473 best. That accepted label does not validate the extra strained ring. The records show alternative arrangements, not an exact missing target pharmacophore or an isolated causal benefit of ring growth.

per_task.generated_character: The output ranges from flexible enamine/urea-like fragments to compact fluorinated fused diones. Optimizer median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings versus Parent 27 and four. The seed-0 best has 23 heavy atoms and one nonaromatic oxygen ring, with multiple unsaturated amino substituents, N-linked nitrile, urea/formyl functionality and a fluoroalkenyl side chain. Seed 1 best has 29 heavy atoms, a fused dione and an eight-membered sulfur/nitrogen ring, plus several fluorines, an N–S–H substituent, direct ring N–F and a fluorohydroxymethyl group. Seed 2 best has 27 heavy atoms and three rings, combining the dione with a cyclopentadiene carboxamide, an N–S–F group and direct amide N–F. Sulfur-containing observations rise from Parent 145 to Child 407 and S–N-containing observations from 35 to 301. The fused diones are recognizable building blocks, but the fluorinated heteroatom attachments and mixed sulfur/nitrogen rings make the complete leaders chemically questionable.
liabilities: Direct N–F on a heterocycle or amide, N–S–F, N–S–H, fluorohydroxymethyl and unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen-ring environments require separate local reactivity and stability assessments.
The flexible seed-0 enamine/urea/formyl family has a different set of hydrolysis and conformational questions; absence of N–F alone does not establish synthetic or pharmacological suitability.
missing_features: Stable, conventional substitutes for the leading heteroatom-fluorine and N–S attachments, preserving the useful size and nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement, are not demonstrated at comparable leading labels. This is an output gap, not proof that those bonds cause the high scores.

The best seed-1 and seed-2 structures have four and one perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, respectively. Their stereochemical forms and the consequences of stereochemical resolution remain unknown.
A universal missing aromatic scaffold or additional fluorine requirement cannot be inferred: the nonaromatic seed-0 family is a material counterexample.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A much larger joined aryl/dione/amide/amine assembly at seed 1 evaluation 15 scores 3.2416258040348776e-69. Child best scores for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.43130179609425895, 0.5830876809861345 and 0.5818858582010464; Parent scores are 0.6942804632817005, 0.4999004646832901 and 0.6201223048692813. The high-score Child decile spans 22–30 heavy atoms and favors smaller organized fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl structures over the oversized assemblies and tiny fragments at the low end. Direct N-halogen bonds appear in 59 of its 87 observations; overall they decrease from Parent 425 to Child 335, while S-halogen observations increase from 3 to 49. The seed-0 nonaromatic leader proves that a fused aromatic dione and heteroatom-halogen attachment are not universal requirements, but its label remains lower than the other Child leaders. The Parent seed-0 high label also contains N–F and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring, so the comparison supplies no clean stable-template answer. Fewer small unsaturated rings, Child 25 versus Parent 224, changes the liability mix rather than establishing better chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fresh observation from n-5277bf3b7425 against code Parent n-1744a1494180, using the complete matched current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 accepted observations per session. Across 4350 optimizer observations, direct N-halogen falls from 786 to 544 and O-halogen from 217 to 89, but S–N rises from 306 to 1050 and sulfur-containing observations from 1100 to 1706. Leading molecules include N–F, N–S–F, N–S–H and constrained N–O connections; other high-label molecules have more conventional thioether or aryl-amine chemistry. An S–N flag also includes ordinary sulfonamides and is not itself a reactivity verdict. This re-observes the environment-dependent bonding gap documented in the Parent assessment; its older sulfur-envelope conditions are not evidence that this Child isolated a sulfur effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional functional-group environments are not consistently preserved while useful molecular arrangements are elaborated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve complete local functional-group environments when editing graphs, and make conventional alternatives to reactive attachments available while retaining useful learned arrangements. Use session feedback to discover where such alternatives matter; do not hard-code a target answer, equate all N–O or S–N bonds with instability, or treat these associations as component attribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fresh source n-5277bf3b7425 versus n-1744a1494180 under the same complete matched Search panel and 300-observation session condition. The Child has 153 optimizer observations with a three-membered ring containing two aromatic atoms, versus Parent 3; a near-leading tertiary-amine molecule carries an oxygen bridge of this kind. Another leading assembly has 24 perceived rings, including eight four-membered closures, and other accepted late structures contain tiny cyclic esters. These are explicit graph observations, not conformer calculations. The broader valence-versus-geometry gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and carried through n-62daf219c70a in the Parent report; those historical settings are not pooled with the present counts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring generation lacks consistent evidence of geometrically credible unsaturation and bridge connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring edits sensitive to bond geometry, ring size and bridge connectivity, and provide feasible alternative topologies that preserve learned functional relationships. Distinguish ordinary small rings and accessible medium rings from strained aromatic bridges; generic ring count or sanitization cannot supply that distinction. Any benefit requires new matched evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This is a current output association from n-5277bf3b7425 compared with n-1744a1494180 on all issued Search seeds and complete 300-observation sessions. In one observed stream the optimizer median grows from 31 to 50 heavy atoms; the Child high-label decile has median 78 heavy atoms versus Parent 32, and a Child leader has 108 heavy atoms and 27 rotatable bonds. The matched Parent has a substantially smaller high-label realization. The same Child stream has 361 distinct generic cores versus Parent 240, including elaborate repeated structures. Other streams retain compact molecules or lose core breadth. Raw core counts therefore describe identities, not productive scaffold discovery, breeding use, mediator effects or an isolated component contribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can multiply familiar ring-bearing fragments without establishing compact, independently useful chemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support size-controlled rearrangement, simplification and genuinely different connectivity alongside fragment recombination, so favorable functional relationships need not be represented by repeated assemblies. Let accepted feedback establish where compact alternatives are useful. Do not impose a universal size optimum from one stream or use scaffold-count growth as a substitute for labelled chemical progress.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fresh re-observation in n-5277bf3b7425 and n-1744a1494180 on the complete current-profile Search panel, 300 accepted observations per session. All digest stereocentre-string incidences are zero. Independent RDKit perception finds unassigned centres in 2464 of 4350 Child optimizer observations versus Parent 2455, with no assigned centres in either set. Both aryl-amine and connected lactam high-label sets contain these unresolved centres; some leaders are achiral under this perception and must remain distinguished. This recurring gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried through n-62daf219c70a in the Parent assessment. The new counts have only the current source and conditions; the records do not show a stereochemical score advantage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic generated structures remain unspecified at the point of evaluation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve chemically meaningful stereochemistry during graph transformations while distinguishing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Keep protonation, tautomerism and conformer questions separate. Neutral strings and absent stereotags cannot establish a unique experimentally realizable molecular form.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
